title: An Isolated Particle Pole for the Two-Dimensional O(3) Spin Field
main_claim: For the continuum O(3) spin field built by the companion paper's lattice prescription, the Källén–Lehmann measure is rho = Z delta_{m1^2} + rho_rest, with Z>0 and supp rho_rest contained in [(m1+delta)^2, infinity). In words, the lowest mass m1 = m_* is an isolated atom.
coverage:
I read every section (1-7) line by line, plus the figure.

Sec 2: inputs and the kernel lemma.

Sec 3: the identity P(w_k)-P(w_{k+1}) = Delta/(4w_k^2); l^p monotonicity of the pressure; g_N, the trace identity and the uniform gap; the slab-insertion norm and torus/cylinder error s(t-r)+s(t); the iterated doubling comparison with the plane; moment comparison by truncation.

Sec 4: the full quadratic covariance bound. This covers the pairing expansion with color-independent d_pi>=0, the bound d_pi<=G^2 (via the rotator unlike-color sign plus alpha-association), the agree/differ single-color trick, and the mixed case. The mixed case uses the conditional-covariance split, Fourier domination |c_k|<=d_k, and the |Cov Y|<=Cov D association argument. I also checked FKG for alpha (signs of the mixed partials), the even-sector norm <= tau^2, and the overlap b >= tau/(1+tau) (algebra checked).

Sec 5: the Edwards–Sokal positive association of (alpha, eta); the trace eigen-expansion lower bound; the cluster-flip argument; Paley–Zygmund for S; the short-way to long-way crossings via Köhler-Schindler–Tassion (KST) RSW in the cutoff plane, plus barrier geometry; the bridge estimate with association; and the final limit order e >= m_* - O(log w / sqrt w).

Sec 6: the exchange identity (rederived; the g(t) terms cancel); the heat-product bound; the Bernstein/Hoeffding polynomial (D b^2 = D^{3/4}, the E_* tail, degree >= t0, coefficient sum 3^D); the pair counting below 2e >= 7m_*/4 > u1+b; and the backward dyadic iteration with summable shifts.

Sec 7: the momentum-projection moment identity and its Riemann sum; the Fourier computation giving |h^(p)|^2 G(E)^2/(2E) e^{-nE} (rederived); the passage from moments to continuous tests via Bernstein polynomials in x; momentum sectors giving J c0 w <= N(u0); and the isolated support point implying an atom.

Not audited: the companion-paper inputs that were imported (O3 paper Props 8.1/8.3/Thm 8.4 defect bound, Prop 10.1 moment majorant, Props 10.2-11.5 OS reconstruction and one-field norm), and the exact hypotheses of the KST theorem, which I took from memory.
sibling_notes: This paper depends on the companion 'The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O3 model'. The board has it as no_gap_found (partial) at rank 71, with its RG step imported from Sharp-mass-bounds-O4 (rank 348), which nobody has audited yet.
